signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 114.28 as the strongest G10 bilateral theme of the week, characterized by a 1.415% performance spread between the leading Loonie and lagging Yen. This divergence is fundamentally supported by a +125bp OIS carry advantage for CAD (CORRA 2.27% vs TONA 0.98%) and a bullish Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +11.6 for Canada against a cooling US backdrop. While the BoC is on hold at 2.25%, the pair remains technically supported as USD/CAD trades below its SMA20/50 cluster (1.4033/1.4075), signaling broad CAD strength. The JPY remains under pressure as the G10 laggard despite elevated producer price inflation at 7.2%, as markets focus on the carry disadvantage. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; carry-positive divergence supported by superior CAD data surprises. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Sharp rise in VIX above 25 triggers a carry unwind, favoring the JPY.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew vs Realized Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.30 is testing the lower bounds of its recent range, positioned below its SMA20 at 160.80 and SMA50 at 161.14. The options market is signaling high alert with a 25d risk reversal (RR) of -2.16, the most aggressive put skew in the G10 space, indicating heavy demand for downside protection. This extreme skew exists despite a negative Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of -1.5%, where implied volatility (7.2%) sits below realized volatility (8.7%), suggesting a potential mispricing of tail risk. Speculative positioning remains heavily short JPY (LF net -63,633), creating a massive squeeze potential if the spot breaks below the SMA200 at 158.15. The +266bp OIS carry advantage continues to support the pair on a nominal basis, but the options market is clearly paying for protection against a carry liquidation. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; extreme options skew signals downside hedging despite positive carry. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Price holds above 160.00 and carry demand resurfaces, forcing the options protection to be unwound.

signals.title: AUD/USD — RBA Hawkishness vs Crowded Positioning
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7062, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6934–0.7016) following hawkish commentary from Assistant Governor Kent. Kent flagged upside inflation risks and signaled that further hikes remain possible, supporting the AUD real rate of +0.60%. However, speculative positioning is now nearing an extreme with COT LF net longs at +37,990 (72.1% long), which is likely to cap the immediate upside. Retail sentiment is currently 80% short, providing a contrarian tailwind as retail fades the institutional long trend. The -71bp OIS carry premium in favor of AUD versus the USD (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%) continues to attract yield-seeking flows as US CPI cooling reduces Fed hike bets. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; supported by RBA hawkishness and retail divergence, though crowded spec longs warrant caution. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Broad risk-off sentiment causes a liquidation of the crowded speculative long position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3499, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3369–1.3423) despite a neutral OIS carry differential (0bp). The options market is pricing in a significant risk premium with 1M ATM implied volatility at 11.0% against a realized HV30 of only 6.0%, resulting in a massive +5.0% Vol Risk Premium (VRP). This suggests traders are paying a steep premium for protection, potentially due to the restrictive real interest rate of +0.93% and upcoming BoE uncertainty. Speculative positioning is moderately long (lev_net +39,039), and the pair remains in a technical uptrend. Given the low VIX environment (14.6), the high GBP vol premium reflects idiosyncratic currency risk rather than broad market stress. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; high vol premium makes directional bets expensive relative to realized movement. Catalyst: BoE meeting 17 Sep. Risk: Sharp compression in VRP if realized volatility catches up to implied pricing.
